summary: The paper isolates prescribed cuspidal pieces of the automorphic L²-spectrum by multipliers of the convolution algebra of Schwartz test functions, and uses this to prove the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1) in the stable case (Theorem 1.8), a nonvanishing theorem for central Rankin–Selberg values (Theorem 1.9) and the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for tempered stable pairs (Theorem 1.10), removing the earlier requirement of a split place where both representations are supercuspidal. §2 constructs multipliers μ⋆ of the Schwartz algebra S(G) of a real reductive group for every W-invariant holomorphic μ of moderate growth along the sets Y*_ϑ attached to the real form (Theorem 2.13), extending Delorme (Appendix A) by difference operators and Kostant's tensor-product theory; §3 combines these with spherical Hecke operators and Donnelly's bound on cuspidal eigenvalues to annihilate every cuspidal component of the coarse Langlands decomposition except those in which a given character occurs (Theorems 3.6, 3.7, 3.19); §4 runs Zydor's Jacquet–Rallis relative trace formulas with multipliers compatible under base change, which preserve smooth transfer (Proposition 4.8), and also proves weak base change for unitary groups without the endoscopic classification (Theorem 4.14). The atlas plans the (g, K)-module foundations (AF.1), finiteness of automorphic forms (AF.2), the spectral decomposition (AS.4), Rankin–Selberg integrals (AL.3), the Mok/KMSW classification (ML.4) and the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent (ML.5); the Gan–Gross–Prasad framework is pending in GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups. Nothing plans Schwartz multipliers, Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula, the isolation theorems, or the Jacquet–Rallis global trace formulas and their comparison beyond the local layers pending in JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (PAPER-ZHANG-21). Nine source issues are recorded; the one of substance is that the proof of Proposition 4.13(1) (archimedean compatibility of weak base change) covers only a cuspidal base change as written, which Theorem 3.19 repairs.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: isolating the nearly isotypic cuspidal part of a non-CAP representation
items.statement: Let F be a number field, G connected reductive over F, K ⊂ G(A_F^∞) open compact, and π = ⊗_v π_v an irreducible admissible representation of G(A_F) with unitary automorphic central character ω. Suppose there is no pair (P, σ), P a proper parabolic subgroup of G and σ a cuspidal automorphic representation of its Levi quotient M(A_F), with π_v a constituent of Ind_P^G(σ_v) for almost all v. Then there is a multiplier μ⋆ of S(G(A_F))_K such that for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K: (1) R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into the π-nearly isotypic subspace L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)_π (the K-invariants of the irreducible subrepresentations π̃ with π̃_v ≅ π_v for almost all v); (2) π(μ⋆f) = π(f).
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; special case of Theorem 3.6 (T = S, χ = χ_{π^T})
items.note: Remark 1.2: it fails for compactly supported test functions; the Schwartz algebra is essential.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: isolating one cuspidal component for Res_{F′/F} GL_n
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.1 with G = Res_{F′/F} GL_n and π an irreducible constituent of Ind_P^G(σ) for a parabolic P and a cuspidal automorphic σ of its Levi quotient: there is a multiplier μ⋆ of S(G(A_F))_K such that R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into the cuspidal component L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) and π(μ⋆f) = π(f).
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.3, p. 2; special case of Theorem 3.19 with strong multiplicity one

items.name: Definition 1.5: conjugate self-dual and hermitian representations of GL_n(A_E)
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F of number fields with involution c and an isobaric automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_E): Π is conjugate self-dual if Π^∨ ≅ Π ∘ c; Π is hermitian if it is an isobaric sum of mutually non-isomorphic cuspidal Π_1, …, Π_d, each conjugate self-dual with L(s, Π_i, As^{(−1)^n}) regular at s = 1.
items.note: Equivalently each Π_i has the conjugate-self-dual sign (−1)^{n−1} of U(n)-parameters; for cuspidal Π exactly one Asai L-function has a pole at s = 1.

items.name: Definition 1.6: weak automorphic base change
items.statement: For a hermitian space V over E of rank n, G = U(V) and an irreducible admissible π of G(A_F), an isobaric automorphic Π of GL_n(A_E) is a weak automorphic base change of π if for almost all places v of F split in E, the split local base change of π_v is isomorphic to Π_v. It is unique up to isomorphism (Ramakrishnan, Theorem A) and denoted BC(π).
items.note: Weaker than the usual notion (no local–global compatibility at nonsplit places), chosen to keep the argument independent of the endoscopic classification of unitary groups.

items.name: Theorem 1.8: the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1), stable case
items.statement: Let Π_n, Π_{n+1} be hermitian cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E), GL_{n+1}(A_E). The following are equivalent: (1) L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0; (2) there are a hermitian space V_n of rank n (with V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ E·e, e of norm 1), for m = n, n+1 irreducible subrepresentations π_m ⊆ A_cusp(G_m), G_m = U(V_m), with BC(π_m) ≅ Π_m, and cusp forms φ_m ∈ π_m with 𝒫(φ_n, φ_{n+1}) = ∫_{G_n(F)∖G_n(A_F)} φ_n(h)φ_{n+1}(h) dh ≠ 0 (Tamagawa measure).
items.note: Previously known when Π_n and Π_{n+1} are supercuspidal at a prime of E split over F (Zhang, Xue, Beuzart-Plessis). Remark 4.17 strengthens (1) ⇒ (2) with archimedean compatibility and hyperspecial fixed vectors.

items.name: Theorem 1.9: a nonvanishing theorem for central Rankin–Selberg values
items.statement: For every hermitian cuspidal automorphic Π_{n+1} of GL_{n+1}(A_E) there is a hermitian cuspidal automorphic Π_n of GL_n(A_E) with L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0.

items.name: Theorem 1.10: the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1), stable tempered case
items.statement: In the situation of (2) of Theorem 1.8, if π_n and π_{n+1} are everywhere tempered, the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture (R. N. Harris's formulation, Conjecture 1.2) holds for π_n and π_{n+1}.
items.note: The proof uses the endoscopic classification of generic packets (Mok, Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White) and the local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture, and then follows Beuzart-Plessis's proof of his Theorem 5 in 'Plancherel formula for GL_n(F)∖GL_n(E)…'.

items.name: The Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for unitary groups (Harris's formulation)
items.statement: (Ichino–Ikeda; R. N. Harris, IMRN 2014, Conjecture 1.2; see also W. Zhang, JAMS 2014, Conjecture 1.1) For everywhere tempered cuspidal π_n ⊠ π_{n+1} of U(V_n) × U(V_{n+1}), an explicit formula for |𝒫(φ_n, φ_{n+1})|² in terms of the central value L(½, BC(π_n) × BC(π_{n+1})), adjoint L-values at s = 1 and normalised local integrals of matrix coefficients over H(F_v); the paper cites the conjecture and does not restate it.
items.note: The GGP candidate's brief reserves the refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjecture for the first consumer that needs it; this paper is that consumer.

items.name: The local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unitary groups (Beuzart-Plessis)
items.statement: (Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418 (archimedean case), as cited for the places in □) For tempered L-parameters of U(n) × U(n+1) over a local field, exactly one member of the Vogan packet has a nonzero H-invariant functional, as predicted; in particular the local Jacquet–Langlands transfer from relevant tempered representations of pure inner forms to stable tempered classes of the quasi-split form is injective.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.9, p. 36; proof of Theorem 1.10, p. 42
items.note: GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups lists this known case ('unitary p-adic and real tempered, Beuzart-Plessis') among its cited theorems.

items.name: Schwartz functions and the Schwartz algebra of a real reductive group
items.statement: For G = G(R), G connected reductive over R, a Schwartz function is a smooth f with Df bounded for every algebraic differential operator D on G (Wallach). S(G) is a Fréchet algebra under convolution; for every Fréchet representation of moderate growth, π(f)v = ∫_G f(g)π(g)v dg converges. S(G) ⊆ ∩_{p>0} 𝒞^p(G) (Harish-Chandra L^p-Schwartz spaces), with equality iff the centre is compact (Remark 2.11). By the Sobolev lemma, S(G) = {f ∈ L²(G) : Df ∈ L²(G) for all D}, with the Fréchet topology given by f ↦ ‖Df‖_{L²} (Remark 2.12). Adelically, S(G(A_F)) := S(G_∞) ⊗ S(G(A_F^∞)) (Definition 3.1).
items.note: Not Mathlib's SchwartzMap (on normed spaces): here the growth is measured by algebraic differential operators on the group.

items.name: Multipliers of an algebra
items.statement: For a complex algebra 𝒮, Mul(𝒮) is the algebra of linear maps μ⋆ : 𝒮 → 𝒮 with μ⋆(f ∗ g) = (μ⋆f) ∗ g = f ∗ (μ⋆g) for all f, g ∈ 𝒮.

items.name: Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2: Weierstrass products of finite rank
items.statement: A subset Λ ⊆ C has rank p if it is countable and p is the least integer ≥ 0 with Σ_{λ∈Λ∖{0}} |λ|^{−(p+1)} < ∞. For such Λ the Weierstrass product Ψ_{Λ,p}(z) = z^δ ∏_{λ≠0} E_p(z/λ), E_p(z) = (1 − z)exp(z + ⋯ + z^p/p), is an entire function of order at most p + 1 with zero set exactly Λ.
items.note: Classical complex analysis; the pinned Mathlib has no Weierstrass factorisation.

items.name: Definition 2.3, Proposition 2.4 and Corollaries 2.5–2.6: holomorphic functions of moderate vertical growth with prescribed zeros
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional real U, a holomorphic μ on U_C has moderate vertical growth if for every M > 0 there is r_M with sup_{‖Re z‖<M} |μ(z)|(1 + ‖z‖)^{r_M} < ∞. (2.4) For a polynomial λ : U_C → C and an entire Ψ of finite order e there is ν of moderate vertical growth with zero set λ^{−1}(Ψ^{−1}(0)) (ν(z) = exp(z_1^{2q} + ⋯ + z_r^{2q})Ψ(λ(z)), q odd > (deg λ)e). (2.5) Hence for Λ ⊆ C of finite rank there is such ν with zero set λ^{−1}Λ. (2.6) For a lattice L ⊆ U_C and a finite A ⊆ U_C there is ν of moderate vertical growth vanishing on L ∖ A and nowhere zero on A.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.3, Proposition 2.4, Corollaries 2.5–2.6 and Remark 2.7, pp. 9–10
items.note: Printed with ν for μ in Definition 2.3 (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Definition 2.8: the spaces of multiplier functions M_θ, N_θ and M^♯_θ
items.statement: For a root datum with Weyl group W, h* = X* ⊗ R, and a W-stable set θ of automorphisms ϑ of order ≤ 2, with h*_ϑ (resp. h*^−_ϑ) the ±1 eigenspaces and Y*_ϑ the projection of ρ + X* to h*^−_ϑ: M_θ(h*_C) is the space of holomorphic μ with sup_{α∈h*_{ϑ,C}, ‖Re α‖<M, ϖ∈Y*_ϑ} |μ(α+ϖ)|(1 + ‖α+ϖ‖)^{r_{ϑ,M}} < ∞ for some r_{ϑ,M}, for all ϑ ∈ θ and M; N_θ(h*_C) requires this for every r (rapid decay); M^♯_θ(h*_C) ⊆ M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C) consists of μ vanishing on h*_{ϑ,C} + ϖ for all but finitely many ϖ ∈ Y*_ϑ, for each ϑ ∈ θ. All are algebras stable under W; M(h*_C) · M^♯_θ ⊆ M^♯_θ (Remark 2.9).

items.name: Lemma 2.10: nonvanishing elements of M^♯_θ
items.statement: For every α_0 ∈ h*_C there is μ ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W with μ(α_0) ≠ 0.
items.note: From Corollary 2.6 applied, for each ϑ, to a lattice of h*^−_{ϑ,C} containing Y*_ϑ.

items.name: The Harish-Chandra isomorphism, infinitesimal characters and Casselman–Wallach representations
items.statement: Z(g) ≅ C[h*_C]^W (Harish-Chandra), so characters of Z(g) are W-orbits in h*_C and μ(χ) makes sense for μ ∈ O(h*_C)^W; admissible representations are smooth admissible Fréchet representations of moderate growth (Casselman–Wallach), equivalent to Harish-Chandra (g, K)-modules by taking K-finite vectors; each irreducible one has an infinitesimal character χ_π.
items.note: AF.1 plans (g, K)-modules, the centre of U(g) with infinitesimal-character subspaces, and the Casselman–Wallach globalisation.

items.name: Theorem 2.13 (= Theorem 1.4): multipliers of the Schwartz algebra of a real reductive group
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive over R, G = G(R), and θ the W-stable set of automorphisms of the root datum of G_C of order ≤ 2 of the form wϑ with ϑ inducing the real form. For every μ ∈ M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W there is a unique linear μ⋆ : S(G) → S(G) with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)·π(f) for every f ∈ S(G) and every irreducible admissible π; in particular μ⋆ ∈ Mul(S(G)). It is continuous and preserves the bi-K-finite functions (Remark 2.26).
items.note: Proof: first for N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W with L²-bounds (Proposition 2.24), then μ_n = exp(−P(α/n))μ with a positive W_θ-invariant homogeneous polynomial P.

items.name: Remarks 2.14–2.17 and Example 2.15: θ_G and the conjectural description of multipliers
items.statement: θ_G ⊆ θ, the set of involutions induced by the maximal tori of G, satisfies: θ_G = θ iff G is quasi-split; 1 ∈ θ_G iff G is split; −1 ∈ θ_G iff G has an anisotropic maximal torus; θ_G = {−1} iff G is anisotropic. Conjecture (Remark 2.16): μ ∈ O(h*_C)^W gives a multiplier as in Theorem 2.13 iff μ ∈ M_{θ_G}(h*_C)^W (known for G anisotropic, for G split by Theorem 2.13, and for SL_2(R) by Barker). For SL_2: M_{±1}^W consists of even entire functions of moderate vertical growth and polynomial growth on Z. Theorem 2.13 gives a homomorphism M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W → Mul(S(G)) (Remark 2.17).

items.name: Lemma 2.18: elements of M^♯_θ see only finitely many K-types
items.statement: For μ ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W there is a finite set 𝔗(μ) of K-types such that every irreducible admissible π with μ(χ_π) ≠ 0 contains a member of 𝔗(μ).
items.note: Proof: Harish-Chandra's discrete series infinitesimal characters leave finitely many (M, σ) up to conjugation and unramified twist; Langlands quotients inherit the minimal K-types of their standard modules (Knapp, Thm. 15.10).

items.name: Discrete series infinitesimal characters and minimal K-types
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra; Vogan, as in Knapp, Theorem 15.10) The infinitesimal characters of discrete series of Levi subgroups are described by Harish-Chandra's parametrisation; for a standard module the Langlands quotient contains its minimal K-types.

items.name: Lemma 2.19: maximal tori give elements of θ
items.statement: For a maximal torus T of G with T = A_T T_c and a universal isomorphism T_C ≅ H inducing h* = a*_T ⊕ i t*_c, there is a unique ϑ ∈ θ with a*_T = h*_ϑ and i t*_c = h*^−_ϑ (ϑ is induced by complex conjugation on T).

items.name: Lemmas 2.20, 2.21 and 2.23: difference operators on holomorphic functions
items.statement: Let W̃ = X* ⋊ W, ℓ_s affine functions vanishing on the fixed hyperplanes of reflections s ∈ W̃, R the algebra generated by translations t_w and multiplication by polynomials, 𝒮 = C[h*_C][ℓ_s^{−1}] ⊗ R and 𝒯 = C(h*_C) ⊗ R. (2.23, after Kostant–Kumar) An element of 𝒯 preserving C[h*_C] lies in 𝒮. (2.21) If μ vanishes on H_s, then p_{ϑ,M,r}(ℓ_s^{−1}μ) ≤ C·p_{ϑ′,M+M_s,r}(μ) for suitable ϑ′ ∈ θ ∪ {1}. (2.20) An S ∈ 𝒮 preserving C[h*_C] extends continuously to O(h*_C) with p_{ϑ,M,r}(Sμ) ≤ C·p_{ϑ,M+M_S,r+r_S}(μ); it preserves N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C), and N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W if it maps C[h*_C] into C[h*_C]^W.
items.note: Lemma 2.21's proof has |u| = 1 where |u| ≤ 1 is needed (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Kostant: tensoring with a finite-dimensional representation
items.statement: (Kostant, J. Funct. Anal. 20 (1975), Thms 4.8 and 4.9) For a finite-dimensional algebraic τ and δ : U(g) → U(g) ⊗ End(W_τ), X ↦ X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ τ(X), the centraliser R_τ of δ(U(g)) is a finitely generated free Z(g)-module, and P_z(δ(z)) = 0 for z ∈ Z(g), where P_z(X) = ∏_{λ∈Λ(τ)} (X − t_λ z).
items.locator: §2.4, before and in the proof of Lemma 2.22, p. 16

items.name: Lemma 2.22: the action of the centre on R_τ by difference operators
items.statement: For every basis v_1, …, v_r of R_τ over Z(g) there are S_1, …, S_r ∈ 𝒮 mapping C[h*_C] to C[h*_C]^W with δ(z) = Σ_i S_i(z) v_i for every z ∈ Z(g).

items.name: Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula and the infinitesimal characters of tempered representations
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra, 1975–76) There is a measure dπ on the tempered dual with ‖f‖²_{L²} = ∫_{Temp(G)} ‖π(f)‖²_{HS} dπ for f ∈ S(G); the infinitesimal characters of tempered representations form exactly ∪_{ϑ∈θ_G} i h*_ϑ ⊕ Y*_ϑ.

items.name: Proposition 2.24: Theorem 2.13 for rapidly decreasing μ, with L²-bounds
items.statement: Theorem 2.13 holds for μ ∈ N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W. Moreover, for every algebraic differential operator D there is M_D > 0 such that for every f ∈ S(G) and r there is C_{D,f,r} with ‖D(μ⋆f)‖_{L²} ≤ C_{D,f,r}·max_{ϑ∈θ} p_{ϑ,M_D,r}(μ) for all such μ.
items.note: Proof: Delorme's multipliers on bi-K-finite functions (Proposition A.1), the Plancherel formula for D = 1, and for polynomial D the identity P(μ⋆f) = Σ S_i(μ) ⋆ P_{ij} L(u_{ij}) f from Lemma 2.22, checked on generic principal series (Lemma 2.25).

items.name: Lemma 2.25: generic principal series tensored with τ are semisimple
items.statement: For a minimal parabolic P_0 = M_0N_0, an irreducible σ of M_0 and ξ an unramified character of M_0 in general position, I_{P_0}^G(σ ⊗ ξ) ⊗ τ is a direct sum of irreducible admissible representations.

items.name: L²-spectrum with central character, quasi-cuspidal test functions
items.statement: For Z the maximal F-split torus in the centre of G and a unitary automorphic character ω of Z(A_F), L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) with right regular action R and cuspidal subspace L²_cusp; S(G(A_F)) acts continuously. f ∈ S(G(A_F)) is ω-quasi-cuspidal if R(f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) into L²_cusp (Definition 3.2).
items.note: AF.3 and AS.4 plan cusp forms and the L²-spectrum; the Schwartz test functions acting on it and quasi-cuspidality are new.

items.name: Definitions 3.3–3.5: T-characters, (G′, T)-CAP characters and T-multipliers
items.statement: For a set T of primes containing S_G (ramified primes), a T-character is χ = (χ_∞, χ^{∞,T}) with χ_∞ a character of Z(g) and χ^{∞,T} of the spherical Hecke algebra H_G^T = ⊗′_{v∉T} C[K_{0,v}∖G(F_v)/K_{0,v}]. For an inner form G′, χ is (G′, T)-CAP if for a proper parabolic P′ of G′ and a cuspidal automorphic σ of M_{P′}(A_F), the spherical representation of χ_v is a constituent of I_{P′}^{G′}(σ_v) for almost all v ∉ T with G_v ≅ G′_v (after Piatetski-Shapiro). A T-multiplier of S(G(A_F))_K is an element of M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W ⊗ H_G^T; it acts as a multiplier since H_G^T is central in S(G(A_F^∞))_K. L²_cusp(…/K, ω)[χ] is the largest closed subspace on which Z(g) ⊗ H_G^T acts by χ.

items.name: Theorem 3.6: isolation for non-CAP characters
items.statement: If χ is not (G, T)-CAP, there is a T-multiplier μ of S(G(A_F))_K with μ(χ) = 1 such that, for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K, R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)[χ]; in particular μ⋆f is ω-quasi-cuspidal.

items.name: Theorem 3.7: isolation inside the cuspidal spectrum
items.statement: For every T-character χ there is a T-multiplier μ with μ(χ) = 1 such that R(μ⋆f) maps L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)[χ] for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K.

items.name: The coarse Langlands decomposition by cuspidal data
items.statement: (Langlands, Lemma 4.6(i); Mœglin–Waldspurger II.2.4) L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) = ⊕̂_{(M,σ)} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) over cuspidal data (M standard Levi, σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω) up to unitary twist and W(G, M_0)-conjugacy; Definition 3.9), each component the closure of the pseudo-Eisenstein series E(g, Φ) = Σ_{γ∈P(F)∖G(F)} Φ̃(γg) of Paley–Wiener sections Φ; components are equal iff the data are equivalent; likewise after taking K-invariants (3.2).
items.note: AS.4 plans the complete spectral decomposition over associate cuspidal data with Eisenstein wave packets; AS.1 the induced families.

items.name: Finiteness of cusp forms with fixed infinitesimal character, K-types and level
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra, LNM 62) There are only finitely many cuspidal automorphic representations of G(A_F), up to isomorphism, with a given infinitesimal character, a given finite set of K_∞-types and nonzero invariants under a given open compact subgroup.
items.note: AF.2 plans the finiteness of automorphic forms with fixed level, finitely many K-types and an infinitesimal-character ideal; AF.3 the finite multiplicity of cuspidal constituents.

items.name: Donnelly: counting cuspidal eigenvalues
items.statement: (Donnelly, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982), Thm. 9.1) For a finite-volume locally symmetric space and a fixed finite set of K-types, the counting function of cuspidal Casimir (Laplace) eigenvalues satisfies a Weyl-type upper bound; as used here, the set of these eigenvalues has finite rank and each eigenvalue has finite multiplicity.
items.note: Remark 3.20 mentions Müller's trace class theorem as the alternative for the Langlands decomposition by discrete data.

items.name: Definition 3.11: χ_∞-typical cuspidal data
items.statement: For a standard Levi M with derived group M_der, b*_M the weight space of the maximal torus of M_der, c*_M = ker(h* → b*_M) ⊇ a*_M, γ_M = γ_M^+ ⊕ γ_M^− : h* → c*_M/a*_M ⊕ b*_M, and λ_M the Casimir polynomial of M_der: σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω)^♥ is χ_∞-typical if γ_M^+(χ_{σ_∞}) ∈ γ_M^+(χ_∞) and λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_{σ_∞})) ∈ λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_∞)). (Remark 3.10: c*_M/a*_M is the cotangent space of Z_M(A_F)^1Z(A_F).)

items.name: Lemmas 3.12–3.14 and Proposition 3.15: killing all but finitely many cuspidal components
items.statement: For fixed K and the finite set 𝔗 of K_∞-types of Lemma 2.18: (3.12) the Casimir values λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_{σ_∞})) for σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M) form a set of finite rank; (3.13) only finitely many classes in 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)^♥ are χ_∞-typical; (3.14) for each standard Levi M there is μ_∞^M ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W with μ_∞^M(χ_∞) ≠ 0 vanishing on the infinitesimal characters χ^G_{σ_s,∞} of Ind_{P_M}^G(σ_{s,∞}) for every non-typical σ and every s ∈ a*_{M,C}; (3.15) μ_∞ = μ_∞^0 ∏_M μ_∞^M ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W has μ_∞(χ_∞) ≠ 0, and R(μ_∞⋆f) annihilates every component L²_{(M,σ)}(…/K, ω) outside the finite set 𝔇(G, ω; K, 𝔗)^♥_{χ_∞}.

items.name: Definition 3.16, Proposition 3.17 and Theorem 3.19: isolating the components in which χ occurs
items.statement: χ occurs in (M, σ) if for some s ∈ a*_{M,C}, χ^G_{σ_s,∞} = χ_∞ and, for every prime v ∉ T, the spherical representation of χ_v is a constituent of Ind_{P_M}^G(σ_{s,v}). (3.17) If χ does not occur in (M, σ), there is a T-multiplier μ_{(M,σ)} with μ_{(M,σ)}(χ) ≠ 0 whose R(μ_{(M,σ)}⋆f) annihilates L²_{(M,σ)}(…/K, ω), built from an exponential-type 'mixed' element ν† of O_exp(h*_C)^W ⊗ H_G^T (after Lindenstrauss–Venkatesh). (3.19) For every T-character χ there is a T-multiplier μ with μ(χ) = 1 such that the image of R(μ⋆f) lies in ⊕_{(M,σ)∈𝔇(G,ω)^♥_χ} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) (a finite sum) for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K.
items.locator: §3.4, Definition 3.16, Proposition 3.17, Theorem 3.19 and proofs, pp. 28–30
items.note: Printed with '(3.9)' for the decomposition (3.2) in Theorem 3.19 (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Remark 3.20: the refinement by the Langlands decomposition
items.statement: Using the Langlands decomposition of L² by discrete data (Langlands; Arthur, Thm. 7.2) and Müller's trace class theorem instead of Donnelly, Theorem 3.19 holds with Langlands components L²_{(M,σ)}(…)′ for discrete automorphic σ; the resulting subspace can be strictly smaller (for PGL_2, the diagonal torus with trivial σ and the trivial representation of G(A_F)).

items.name: Delorme's multipliers for semisimple groups
items.statement: (Delorme, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986), Théorème 1.7) For G semisimple, linear and connected, every μ ∈ N(h*_C)^W gives a linear map μ⋆ : C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} → S(G)_{(K)} with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)π(f) for all irreducible admissible π. (Delorme 1984: for G without compact factors, only polynomials give multipliers of C_c^∞(G), and only exponential-type functions give multipliers of C_c^∞(G)_{(K)}.)

items.name: Proposition A.1: Delorme's theorem for reductive groups
items.statement: For G = G(R) connected reductive and every μ ∈ N(h*_C)^W there is a unique linear μ⋆ : C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} → S(G)_{(K)} with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)·π(f) for every f and every irreducible admissible π.
items.locator: Appendix A, Proposition A.1 and proof, pp. 43–45
items.note: Printed with N(h*_C) for N(h*_C)^W (sourceIssues E8). Reduction to G^0 = (Z^0 × G^0_der)/Z^0_der, with Delorme for G^0_der and Sakellaridis for Z^0, then projective tensor products for fixed K-types and supports.

items.name: Lemma A.2 and its inputs: Paley–Wiener for split tori and tensor products of Schwartz spaces
items.statement: N(z*_C) ⊗̂ N(h*_{der,C})^W ≅ N(h*_C)^W, from the Paley–Wiener isomorphisms S(A) ≅ N(a*_C) for split real tori A (Fourier transform) and S(A_1 × A_2) = S(A_1) ⊗̂ S(A_2) (Aizenbud–Gourevitch, Cor. 2.6.3, for Schwartz functions on Nash manifolds, also used to approximate by pure tensors in §4); with Sakellaridis's multipliers on the centre (Thm. 2.1.2) and the extension of separately continuous bilinear maps on Fréchet spaces to projective tensor products (Trèves, Thm. 34.1).
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.2 and proof, p. 44; §4.2, pp. 34–35

items.name: The Jacquet–Rallis setup: groups, subgroups and regular semisimple orbits
items.statement: For E/F quadratic with character η_{E/F}: G′ = Res_{E/F}GL_n × Res_{E/F}GL_{n+1} with H′_1 the graph of GL_n → GL_{n+1} and H′_2 = GL_{n,F} × GL_{n+1,F}, the character η = (η^{n−1} ∘ det) ⊠ (η^n ∘ det) of H′_2(A_F), regular semisimple γ (H′_1γH′_2 closed with free action) and B′ = H′_1∖G′/H′_2; for V = (V_n, V_{n+1}) in the set 𝔙 of pairs of hermitian spaces with V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ Ee, G^V = U(V_n) × U(V_{n+1}) with the diagonal H^V and B^V = H^V∖G^V/H^V. B′ ≅ B^V canonically, defining matching pairs.
items.note: After Jacquet–Rallis and W. Zhang (Ann. Math. 2014, §3.1).

items.name: Global relative characters and relative orbital integrals
items.statement: For cuspidal Π of G′ and π^V of G^V: I_Π(f′) = Σ_{φ∈B(Π)} (∫_{H′_1(F)∖H′_1(A)} Π(f′)φ) · conj(∫_{Z′(A)H′_2(F)∖H′_2(A)} φ η), J_{π^V}(f^V) = Σ_φ (∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A)} π^V(f^V)φ) · conj(∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A)} φ) (Beuzart-Plessis, §3.1); for regular semisimple γ, δ^V the relative orbital integrals O_η(γ, f′) = ∫∫ f′(h_1^{−1}γh_2)η(h_2) and O(δ^V, f^V) = ∫∫ f^V(h_1^{−1}δ^V h_2), and in general Zydor's regularised I_γ, J_{δ^V}.

items.name: Propositions 4.1–4.2: Zydor's Jacquet–Rallis relative trace formulas for quasi-cuspidal Schwartz functions
items.statement: (Zydor, J. reine angew. Math. 762 (2020), Théorèmes 5.9–5.10, 6.6–6.7, extended to Schwartz test functions) For quasi-cuspidal f′ ∈ S(G′(A_F)): Σ_{Π∈𝔆(G′,1)} I_Π(f′) = Σ_{γ∈B′(F)} I_γ(f′); for quasi-cuspidal f^V ∈ S(G^V(A_F)): Σ_{π^V} J_{π^V}(f^V) = Σ_{δ^V∈B^V(F)} J_{δ^V}(f^V); all sums absolutely convergent.
items.note: The paper asserts that Zydor's proofs for C_c^∞ work for Schwartz functions. The text after (4.4) says I_γ for J_{δ^V} (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Definitions 4.3–4.4: relative hyperspecial subgroups and smooth transfer
items.statement: At v unramified in E, K′_v = GL_n(O_{E_v}) × GL_{n+1}(O_{E_v}) and K^V_v = U(L_n) × U(L_{n+1}) (L_n self-dual, L_{n+1} = L_n ⊕ O_{E_v}e) are relative hyperspecial. f′_□ and f^V_□ have matching orbital integrals if O(δ^V, f^V_□) = Ω_□(γ)·O_η(γ, f′_□) for matching regular semisimple pairs (Ω a transfer factor); f′ and f^V are smooth transfer if they are unit functions of relative hyperspecial subgroups outside a finite □ and match on □; complete smooth transfer if f′ and every f^V match (almost all f^V zero).

items.name: The Jacquet–Rallis relative fundamental lemma
items.statement: (Yun, Duke Math. J. 156 (2011) (large p); Beuzart-Plessis, arXiv:1901.02653 (all p)) At a place v unramified in E, 1_{K′_v} and 1_{K^V_v} have matching orbital integrals; so Definition 4.4(2) does not depend on □ (Remark 4.5).

items.name: Proposition 4.6: existence of smooth transfer
items.statement: (W. Zhang, Thm. 2.6 (nonarchimedean); H. Xue, Thm. 2.7 (archimedean)) At every place v there are dense subspaces S_tr(G′(F_v)) ⊆ S(G′(F_v)) and S_tr(G^{V_v}(F_v)) ⊆ S(G^{V_v}(F_v)), equal to the whole spaces if v is nonarchimedean or split in E, whose elements have smooth transfers: every f′_v ∈ S_tr has matching (f_v^{V_v})_{V_v}, and every f_v^{V_v} ∈ S_tr has a matching f′_v with f^{W_v}_v = 0 for W_v ≠ V_v.

items.name: Proposition 4.7 (Chaudouard–Zydor): equality of the geometric sides
items.statement: (Chaudouard–Zydor, Compos. Math. 157 (2021), Théorème 16.2.4.1, extended from pure tensors) If f′ and (f^V)_V are complete smooth transfer, then Σ_{γ∈B′(F)} I_γ(f′) = Σ_{V∈𝔙} Σ_{δ^V∈B^V(F)} J_{δ^V}(f^V), the sum over V being finite.

items.name: Beuzart-Plessis: local Plancherel formulas and matching of relative characters
items.statement: (Beuzart-Plessis, 'Plancherel formula for GL_n(F)∖GL_n(E) and applications…', Invent. Math. 2021, (5.5.10), (5.5.3), Thms 5.4.1 and 5.4.3) For local test functions, ∫_{B′_rss} O_η(γ, f′_1) conj(O_η(γ, f′_2)) dγ and ∫_{B^V_rss} O(δ, f^V_1) conj(O(δ, f^V_2)) dδ equal spectral integrals of products of local relative characters I_{BC(π)} and J_π against explicit Plancherel measures (|γ*(0, π, Ad, ψ′)|/|S_π| and μ*_{G^V}); matching orbital integrals imply matching relative characters κ_V J_π(f^V) = I_{BC(π)}(f′), the measures agree under the local Jacquet–Langlands map, and κ_V conj(κ_V) = |τ|^{n(n−1)/2}.
items.note: At primes inert in E this relies on Mok and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White (Remark 4.10).

items.name: Lemma 4.9: matching orbital integrals versus matching relative characters
items.statement: Let □ contain all archimedean places and only primes split in E. For f′ ∈ S(G′(F_□)) and f^V ∈ S(G^V(F_□)): f′ and f^V have matching orbital integrals iff κ_{V_□} J_π(f^V) = I_{BC(π)}(f′) for every π ∈ Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□).
items.note: Remark 4.10: the same holds for inert primes in □, using Mok and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White.

items.name: Proposition 4.8: multipliers compatible with base change preserve smooth transfer
items.statement: With T = S ∪ T_0 (T_0 the primes nonsplit in E), the base change maps bc^V_∞ : O(h′*_C)^{W′} → O(h^{V*}_C)^{W^V} (restriction along h^{V*} ⊆ h′*) and bc^T_V : H^T_{G′} → H^T_{G^V}, and bc^V = bc^V_∞ ⊗ bc^T_V: if f′ = ⊗f′_v and f^V = ⊗f^V_v match at every place and μ^V = bc^V(μ′) for T-multipliers μ′, μ^V, then μ′⋆f′ and μ^V⋆f^V are smooth transfer.

items.name: Proposition 4.11: Gaussian test functions at compact archimedean places
items.statement: At an archimedean place v nonsplit in E with V_v positive definite, S_tr(G^{V_v}(F_v)) contains every f^{V_v}_v with J_{π_v}(f^{V_v}_v) = 0 for all but finitely many tempered π_v.
items.note: Not used in the paper; it gives the Gaussian test functions of Rapoport–Smithling–Zhang. The proof writes J_{π_0}(f^V) = 1 for J_{π_0}(f^V_1) = 1 (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Lemma 4.12: choosing T-multipliers compatible under base change
items.statement: Given T-multipliers μ′ of S(G′(A_F))_{K′} and μ^V of S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V} (V ∈ 𝔙°_{(S)}) with μ′(χ′) = 1 = μ^V(χ^V), there are T-multipliers μ̃′ = (multiple of μ′), μ̃^V = (multiple of μ^V) with μ̃′(χ′) = 1 = μ̃^V(χ^V) and μ̃^V = bc^V(μ̃′), namely μ̃′ = (μ′)² ∏_V cb^V((μ^V)²) for linear sections cb^V of bc^V.

items.name: Positive-type test functions and the Burger–Sarnak trick
items.statement: (W. Zhang, Ann. Math. 2014, Propositions 2.12 and 2.14) Local test functions of positive type exist with J_{π_v}(f_v) > 0 when the local period is nonzero; and for cuspidal π_{n+1} of U(V_{n+1}) there is a cuspidal π_n of U(V_n), supercuspidal at a prescribed split prime, with nonzero period 𝒫 on π_n ⊠ π_{n+1} (and π_{n+1} generic or supercuspidal there if π_{n+1} is).
items.locator: §4.3, proofs of Proposition 4.13 and Theorem 4.14, pp. 38–39; §4.4, p. 42

items.name: Flicker: distinction and poles of Asai L-functions
items.statement: (Flicker, Bull. SMF 116 (1988)) A cuspidal Π of GL_m(A_E) has a nonzero period over GL_m(A_F) twisted by η^{m+1}_{E/F} iff L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^{m+1}}) has a pole at s = 1.
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Proposition 4.13, p. 39; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 41

items.name: Strong multiplicity one for GL_n with a density-zero exceptional set
items.statement: (Ramakrishnan, arXiv:1806.08429, Theorem A) Isobaric automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E) that agree at the places above almost all primes of F split in E are isomorphic.
items.locator: §1.2, Definition 1.6, p. 3; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 41
items.note: PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B routed Jacquet–Shalika's strong multiplicity one to LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2; the review should give strong multiplicity one for GL_n one owner.

items.name: Proposition 4.13: weak base change from nonvanishing periods
items.statement: Let V ∈ 𝔙_{(S)} and π^V ∈ 𝔆(G^V, 1) with 𝒫(φ) = ∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A_F)} φ ≠ 0 for some φ ∈ L²(G^V, π^V), and assume (a) π^V is not (G^V, T)-CAP, or (b) π^V_{v_0} is supercuspidal at some prime v_0 split in E. Then the weak base change Π = BC(π^V) = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} exists; (1) the base change of χ_{π^V_∞} is χ_{Π_∞}; (2) in case (b), Π_m is cuspidal and hermitian.
items.note: The proof of (1) as written covers only the case where Π is cuspidal (sourceIssues E1); Theorem 3.19 closes it.

items.name: Theorem 4.14: weak base change for unitary groups without endoscopy
items.statement: Let V° be a hermitian space, G° = U(V°) and π an irreducible admissible representation of G°(A_F). (1) If π is cuspidal automorphic and π_v is generic at infinitely many primes split in E, BC(π) exists. (2) If π is cuspidal automorphic and supercuspidal at some prime split in E, BC(π) exists and is cuspidal and hermitian. (3) If BC(π) exists and is hermitian, π is not (G•, T_0)-CAP for any pure inner form G• of G°. (4) If BC(π) exists and is hermitian, the base change of χ_{π_∞} is χ_{BC(π)_∞}.
items.locator: §4.3, Theorem 4.14 and proof, pp. 39–40; Remarks 1.7 and 4.15
items.note: By induction on rank with the Burger–Sarnak trick and Proposition 4.13; independent of the endoscopic classification (which also implies it). (3) is consistent with Jiang's CAP conjecture. (4) rests on Proposition 4.13(1) (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Lemma 4.16: descent of hermitian representations to quasi-split unitary groups
items.statement: For a hermitian isobaric Π of GL_m(A_E) and V of rank m with U(V) quasi-split, there is a cuspidal π of U(V)(A_F) which is unramified at the split primes where Π is, with base change of χ_{π_v} equal to χ_{Π_v} there; hence Π ≅ BC(π) and the base change of χ_{π_∞} is χ_{Π_∞}.
items.note: Existence by the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent; the archimedean statement by Theorem 4.14(4).

items.name: The Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry automorphic descent
items.statement: (Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry, 2011) The descent from GL_m to classical and unitary groups constructs, for a hermitian isobaric Π, a cuspidal automorphic representation of the quasi-split unitary group whose unramified components correspond to those of Π.
items.note: ML.5 registers the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent among known transfers (as TwistedAutomorphicDescents, from PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20, imports it).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg periods and central values for GL_n × GL_{n+1}
items.statement: (Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika) For cuspidal Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1}, the H′_1-period ∫_{H′_1(F)∖H′_1(A_F)} φ is the Rankin–Selberg zeta integral at s = ½; some cusp form with prescribed unramified components has nonzero period iff L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0.
items.note: AL.3 plans the GL_n × GL_m Rankin–Selberg integrals with their unfolding and unramified computation.

items.name: The endoscopic classification of unitary groups
items.statement: (Mok; Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White) The endoscopic classification of representations of quasi-split unitary groups and their inner forms, used for generic packets in the proof of Theorem 1.10 and for Lemma 4.9 at inert primes.
items.locator: §4.2, Remark 4.10, p. 36; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.10, p. 42
items.note: ML.4 owns the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs.

items.name: §4.4: proofs of Theorems 1.8–1.10 and Remark 4.17
items.statement: (2) ⇒ (1): π^V is not CAP (Theorem 4.14(3)), so the argument of Proposition 4.13(a) with isolating multipliers compatible under base change gives I_Π(μ′⋆f′) ≠ 0, hence a nonzero H′_1-period and L(½, Π) ≠ 0. (1) ⇒ (2): with f′ from Flicker and Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika, I_Π(f′) ≠ 0; descend χ′ = χ_{Π^T} to each V ∈ 𝔙_{(S)} (Lemma 4.16), isolate on both sides (Theorem 3.6, Lemma 4.12, Proposition 4.8), and run Propositions 4.1, 4.7, 4.2 to find π on some G^V with J_π(f^V) ≠ 0. Theorem 1.9 from the Burger–Sarnak trick and Theorem 4.14(2). Remark 4.17: in (2) one may also ask for archimedean compatibility and hyperspecial fixed vectors.
